item.title: Co--dsorption of terrylene and tetrapentacontane on hexagonal boron nitride - towards a two-dimensional Shpolskii matrix
item.description: arXiv:2610.40733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Organic molecular emitters are promising building blocks for quantum technologies, but their use at two-dimensional interfaces is limited by diffusion, aggregation, and photobleaching. We present work towards constructing an ultrathin two-dimensional Shpolskii-like host-guest matrix on hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) by co-depositing terrylene fluorophores with the long-chain tetrapentacontane in a solution-phase process. We demonstrate that this approach disperses terrylene in a roughly one-nanometer-thin alkane layer without detectable phase separation and allows tuning the emitter density from ensembles to isolated emitters showing characteristic blinking behavior consistent with single-molecule fluorescence. Time-lapse confocal microscopy, autocorrelation analysis, and fluorescence recovery after photobleaching show that suppressed diffusion and stable emitter positions can be achieved in several samples with a tetrapentacontane matrix. Encapsulation with hBN from the top side further improves photostability, with emitters demonstrating long lifetimes despite high photon doses. Successful co-adsorption of isolated emitters and alkane matrix is a milestone towards extending Shpolskii-type molecular isolation to hBN and provides a route towards stable, interface-integrated molecular qubits.
item.dc:creator: Rong Sun, Tolibjon Abdurakhmonov, Jan-Niklas Heidkamp, Julian Schr\"oer, Paul Weinbrenner, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Tobias Korn, Oliver K\"uhn, Friedemann Reinhard

item.title: Subsonic terahertz plasmon instability in space-time plasmonic crystals
item.description: arXiv:2610.40880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate collective plasma-wave dynamics in a two-dimensional electron fluid subected to a travelling periodic modulation of the effective plasma velocity. Using a hydrodynamic description combined with Floquet-Bloch theory, we show that the travelling modulation acts as a moving plasmonic crystal whose band structure is governed by an effective drift velocity in the comoving frame. We demonstrate that the closure of the Bragg gap at the edge of the Brillouin zone gives rise to an exceptional point and triggers a Krein-type instability through the coupling of positive- and negative-energy modes. Analytical expressions are derived for the instability threshold and growth rate, revealing that self-amplification can occur even when the electron drift remains subsonic in the laboratory frame. Numerical simulations of the nonlinear hydrodynamic equations confirm the theoretical predictions and show the evolution towards a saturated regime dominated by a coherent Floquet-Bloch mode. These results identify travelling plasmonic crystals as a novel platform for wave amplification and non-Hermitian band dynamics in electronic fluids.
item.dc:creator: H. Ter\c{c}as, J. L. Figueiredo, P. Cosme

item.title: The spin-transfer inverse Faraday effect in Au/YIG thin film bilayers
item.description: arXiv:2610.41061v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The inverse Faraday effect (IFE) (the generation of an effective magnetic field in a material upon irradiation with circularly polarized light) offers a pathway to ultrafast, non-thermal control of spin dynamics. In metallic/ferromagnetic-insulator (NM/FMI) bilayers, IFE-driven spin polarization in the metallic layer can be an alternative to generate magnon excitations in the magnetic insulator which otherwise would be inaccessible with photon energies below the insulator bandgap, but this avenue has remained mostly unexplored. In this work, we investigate the regime of spin-transfer via IFE in Au/YIG bilayers, by means of ultrafast time-resolved magneto-optical experiments. Understanding the mechanism of this spin-transfer IFE in these NM/FMI heterostructures is crucial for several reasons: it elucidates the fundamental coupling between light's angular momentum and collective spin modes at buried interfaces, it enables all-optical generation and manipulation of pure spin currents, and it paves the way toward THz-frequency spintronic devices leveraging the insulator's long magnon lifetimes.
item.dc:creator: Victor H. Ortiz, Daniel Russell, Fengyuan Yang, Roland K. Kawakami

item.title: Anisotropic Boltzmann transport in a tight-binding superlattice: Exact results for power-law energy-dependent scattering
item.description: arXiv:2610.41101v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a complete Boltzmann transport theory for the in-plane ($\sigma_{xx}$) and out-of-plane ($\sigma_{zz}$) conductivities of an electronic superlattice consisting of a periodic stack of two-dimensional (2D) parabolic-band layers coupled along the superlattice axis by nearest-neighbor tunneling $t$, in the physically relevant regime $t\ll E_F$ where the Fermi surface is an open, corrugated cylinder. Within the relaxation-time approximation with a power-law energy-dependent scattering time $\tau(E)\propto E^{p}$, we study the seven models $p=0,\pm1,\pm3/2,\pm2$ as functions of the 2D electron density $n$ per layer and temperature $T$. For $p=-2$ (in plane) and $p\le -1$ (out of plane), long-lived carriers at the miniband bottom can dominate transport at finite temperature. For $p=-2$, these carriers produce a pronounced peak in $\sigma_{zz}(T)$ at $T\sim E_F$. We find that the temperature dependence of the anisotropic metallic dc conductivity can be highly counterintuitive depending on $t$, $T$, and $p$, with no generic increase or decrease with temperature. The Lorenz ratio is determined by the energy variance of the current-carrying electrons; the Wiedemann-Franz (WF) law is exact as $T\to0$ for all models at fixed $t$, with anisotropic corrections at finite temperature. Band-edge carriers first enhance the interlayer Lorenz ratio up to several times its low-temperature value through thermal occupation of separated energy ranges within the same electron band and then suppress it at high temperature by energy filtering. Strong violations of the Wiedemann-Franz law can therefore arise from miniband structure and energy-dependent elastic scattering alone.
item.dc:creator: Sankar Das Sarma, Yuqing Lin

item.title: Quantum-Geometric Subgap Second-Harmonic Generation in PT-Symmetric Antiferromagnetic Insulators
item.description: arXiv:2610.41167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although quantum geometry plays an established role in electronic transport and optical responses, the contribution of the time-reversal-odd Riemannian connection to fully subgap responses remains less explored. Here we identify intrinsic second-harmonic generation in PT-symmetric antiferromagnets, predominantly governed by the real sector of the interband Hermitian connection and arising entirely from virtual interband transitions. In bilayer MnBi$_2$Te$_4$, the response persists in trivial phases but is enhanced in the layer-Chern phase and reverses sign with N\'eel order, offering a probe of quantum geometry and phase-sensitive readout of antiferromagnetic order without mobile carriers or real excitations.
item.dc:creator: Shakeel Ahmad, Fei Xue

item.title: Berry curvature quadrupole induced third-order anomalous Hall effect in altermagnetic $\mathrm{KV_2Se_2O}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.41274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Altermagnets combine compensated magnetic order with momentum-dependent spin splitting, providing a symmetry-rich platform for exploring nonlinear quantum-geometric transport. In the d-wave altermagnet considered here, the antiunitary symmetry operation $TC_{4z}$ enforces a vanishing momentum-integrated Berry curvature, while inversion symmetry forbids a finite Berry-curvature dipole. Consequently, the Berry curvature quadrupole (BCQ) can provide a contribution to the nonlinear Hall response, scaling as $\tau^2$, where $\tau$ denotes the relaxation time. We derive a gauge-covariant Wannier interpolation formula that enables efficient evaluation of the BCQ directly from first-principles Wannier tight-binding Hamiltonians. Applying this framework to $\mathrm{KV_2Se_2O}$, we calculate the momentum-space distribution of the BCQ and the associated chemical potential dependent nonlinear conductivity. The momentum-resolved analysis reveals that the dominant contribution originates from spin-orbit coupling induced avoided arossings, directly linking the gap structure to the sign-changing nonlinear response. Our work establishes a general first-principles route to higher-order quantum-geometric responses in altermagnets, opening avenues for exploring nonlinear Hall effects in next-generation spintronic and magnetoelectronic devices.
item.dc:creator: Jiacheng Yao, Zhuocheng Lu, Zhichao Guo, Hua Wang

item.title: Spin-conserving and spin-flip magnetic scattering in the altermagnetic spin-splitter effect
item.description: arXiv:2610.41414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Critical magnetic fluctuations scatter electrons strongly near an ordering transition, but they barely degrade the charge current, because they scatter mostly through small angles. In an altermagnet the electric field also drives a spin current, and a nearly forward spin flip moves an electron to the other spin band at almost unchanged velocity. We develop a Boltzmann theory of the spin splitter ratio that keeps the full collision operator of quasistatic magnetic fluctuations and its change with the magnetic order. Fluctuations of equal total strength give the same resistivity for every fraction of spin flips, yet they can move the spin splitter ratio in opposite directions. Spin conserving fluctuations relax the spin current at about the charge relaxation rate, whereas forward flips equalize the two spin populations at equal energy at the quasiparticle rate, which in two dimensions grows linearly with the correlation length. Energy conservation on the split bands protects the part of the spin current carried by the band shift of the occupied states at every scattering strength, and the splitting blocks forward flips once the spin Fermi lines lie farther apart than the inverse correlation length. When flips dominate, a quarter to a half of the lattice band ratio survives. The transport time approximation reproduces the initial growth of the resistivity but recovers only a quarter to a half of the initial fall of the ratio, and a disorder series at fixed reduced temperature measures this fall independent of the order amplitude.
item.dc:creator: Yunxi Jiang, Hao Yu

item.title: Spin conservation protects the altermagnetic spin-splitter current from critical scattering
item.description: arXiv:2610.41419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Near a magnetic transition, critical fluctuations scatter electrons strongly, but the charge current survives, because long wavelength fluctuations barely turn the electron velocity. In an altermagnet the electric field also drives a spin current, the spin splitter effect, and a nearly forward scattering event that flips spin moves an electron to the other spin band at almost unchanged velocity. We show that the spin current shares the protection of the charge current only when the fluctuations conserve spin. Solving the Boltzmann equation with the full collision operator, including its change with the magnetic order, we find that forward flips equalize the two spin populations at equal energy at the quasiparticle rate, which in two dimensions grows linearly with the correlation length, whereas spin conserving fluctuations relax the spin current at a rate comparable to the charge relaxation rate. Fluctuations with the same resistivity can thus move the spin splitter ratio in opposite directions. Energy conservation protects the part of the spin current that follows the band shift of the occupied states, and the splitting blocks forward flips once the spin Fermi lines lie farther apart than the inverse correlation length. A disorder series at fixed reduced temperature measures the initial fall of the ratio with the magnetic resistivity independent of the order amplitude, and the growth of this slope toward the transition identifies spin flip critical fluctuations.
item.dc:creator: Yunxi Jiang, Hao Yu

item.title: Potentials of individual atoms by convergent beam electron diffraction
item.description: arXiv:2610.41513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In convergent beam electron diffraction (CBED) on two-dimensional (2D) materials, the intensity distributions within the individual CBED spots map the local atomic arrangements within the probed region. In this study we demonstrate that the average intensities within the CBED spots essentially depend on the scattering parameters by a single atom, thus, offering the possibility of the direct measurement of such parameters. Scattering potential of an individual atom can be approximated by the Gaussian function and its parameters, the standard deviation and the maximal phase shift, can be recovered from the ratio of the intensities in the zero- and higher orders spots in CBED pattern. In order to demonstrate this, we simulated CBED patterns and extracted the atomic scattering parameters from such patterns. In the simulated examples, no weak phase object approximation is applied and the proposed method provides accurate results even for materials with large phase shifts up to 1.5 rad, as for example tungsten. The scattering parameters recovered from the experimental CBED patterns of graphene and twisted graphene-hBN structure show good agreement with the theoretically obtained values.
item.dc:creator: Tatiana Latychevskaia, Colin Robert Woods, Yi Bo Wang, Matthew Holwill, Eric Prestat, Sara Mustafi, Sarah J. Haigh, Kostya S. Novoselov

item.title: Hierarchy of Electromagnetic Gauge Field Quantum Geometries
item.description: arXiv:2610.41610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The conventional Bloch quantum geometric tensor (QGT) describes electric-dipole geometry for spatially uniform perturbations and vertical Bloch transitions. We develop a broader framework linking quantum geometry to local and nonlocal electromagnetic response in gauge-field space, placing this tensor within a hierarchy of electric and magnetic multipole quantum geometries. The intrinsic antisymmetric adiabatic response in every electromagnetic channel is a Berry curvature in the space of its conjugate fields. The field-dependent projector uniquely fixes the QGT for that channel, pairing the response curvature with a quantum metric. This construction extends to spatially nonuniform perturbations, whose finite momentum transfer induces nonvertical Bloch transitions. We explicitly construct the current--current QGT connecting Bloch states at $\mathbf{k}\pm\mathbf{q}/2$, providing a unified metric and curvature description of nonlocal current response. In the doubled Brillouin zone, tangential derivatives generate conventional momentum-space QGT multipoles, whereas normal derivatives connect finite-momentum geometry to uniform electric- and magnetic-multipole-pair QGTs. We derive this connection through second order in $\mathbf{q}$. The finite-momentum curvature governs the intrinsic nonlocal Hall response, while an inverse-frequency moment of symmetric optical absorption probes the index-symmetric metric sector.
item.dc:creator: Bin Wang, Fuming Xu, Lei Zhang, Jian Wang

item.title: Evaluating Instrument-Centered AI Agents for Table-Top Science Experiments
item.description: arXiv:2610.41717v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reliable evaluation of AI agents for table-top science experiments has remained elusive because live instruments are hard to reset and share at scale, while instrument statefulness and safety constraints complicate evaluation. We introduce instrMCP and q-devBench, an evaluation stack for instrument-centered AI agents in table-top experiments. instrMCP connects coding agents to scientific instruments through the Model Context Protocol, serving as the instrument-access harness. q-devBench reconstructs 37 real experimental tasks from condensed-matter physics as virtual QCoDeS instruments covering quantum electronic transport, scanning probe imaging, and calibration workflows. q-devBench exposes reproducible failure modes in laboratory-agent systems while preserving realistic instrument-control workflows. Across a range of commercial coding-agent configurations, current systems already show substantial operational competence, satisfying 70-83% of measurement-related rubric criteria. The main bottleneck is scientific analysis, where performance falls to 28-46%. In an analysis-only ablation in which agents receive clean reference datasets without running the virtual measurement session, analysis performance improves substantially, closing roughly two thirds of the difference between the measurement and analysis scores. This suggests that much of the deficit arises from the measurement-session context, including tool-use overhead, longer context, measurement-planning decisions, and possible acquisition errors, while a residual scientific-reasoning gap remains. Together, instrMCP and q-devBench provide a practical sandbox for benchmarking, diagnosing, and improving laboratory AI harnesses, and establish a route from controlled virtual evaluation to future live-hardware validation.
item.dc:creator: Jiaqi Cai, Siyu Cheng, William S. Huxter, Li-Qiao Xia, Shuwen Sun, Shuai Yuan, Yifan Zhao, Naiyuan Zhang, Weijie Li, Muxian Xu, Ilija Zeljkovic, Xiaodong Xu, Pablo Jarillo-Herrero

item.title: Dipolar Exciton Polarons in a van der Waals Homobilayer
item.description: arXiv:2610.41730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fermi polarons exemplify how many-body interactions give rise to emergent quasiparticles, providing a fundamental framework for understanding interacting quantum matter. In electron-doped two-dimensional semiconductors, exciton polarons offer optical access to Fermi-polaron physics and electrical tunability, yet achieving stronger and more controllable exciton-electron interactions remains a key challenge. Here, we realize dipolar exciton polarons in an electrically tunable van der Waals homobilayer, where interlayer excitons with spatially separated electrons and holes act as quantum impurities carrying permanent electric dipole moments. These dipolar polarons exhibit substantially enhanced exciton-electron interactions, with binding energies more than four times those of conventional intralayer exciton polarons. We further demonstrate that Fermi-sea layer polarization provides an additional degree of freedom for controlling many-body interactions. In particular, the presence of a Fermi sea induces hybridization between oppositely oriented dipolar polarons, whereas confining the Fermi sea to a single layer suppresses this hybridization and produces orientation-selective many-body dressing. Our findings establish an experimental platform for dipolar-polaron physics in which dipole orientation and Fermi-sea layer polarization jointly govern many-body interactions, opening a route towards electrically tunable interactions and dipolar-polaron-mediated attraction between itinerant electrons.
item.dc:creator: Yuxin Duan, Hongming Zhang, Yaofeng Zhu, Hang Zhou, Xinyue Zhang, Yan Liu, Song Luo, Long Zhang, Zhanghai Chen

item.title: Andreev-Enhanced Conductance in a Bilayer Graphene Quantum Point Contact
item.description: arXiv:2610.41915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum point contacts provide a platform for probing mode-dependent Andreev reflection. Here, we demonstrate Andreev-enhanced conductance in a gate-defined bilayer graphene quantum point contact coupled to a superconducting aluminum electrode. Electrostatic gating enables sequential mode occupation, verified by normal-state conductance quantization. In the superconducting state, the conductance is enhanced within the conductance plateaus, while the enhancement decreases between plateaus, consistent with the nonlinear transmission dependence of Andreev reflection. The enhancement yields effective transmission probabilities up to 0.9, and extends over a bias window of approximately 140 $\mu$V, which we associate with a proximity-induced superconducting gap, close to the gap of the aluminum film. For in-plane fields, the enhancement persists up to the critical field, and the bias window follows the spectral gap predicted by Abrikosov-Gor'kov theory. In contrast, perpendicular fields suppress the enhancement approximately linearly from zero field, deviating from homogeneous pair breaking and indicative of flux penetration.
item.dc:creator: Emma Horgan, Bernd Aichner, Nadine Omar, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Luca Banszerus

item.title: Observation of light-induced Haldane gap in graphene
item.description: arXiv:2610.42115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Symmetry and topology, encoded in electronic wavefunctions, play a central role in the electronic properties and emergent phenomena of quantum materials. While these properties are conventionally determined by the equilibrium Hamiltonian, strong optical fields offer a fundamentally different route by reshaping the Hamiltonian on ultrafast timescales, turning symmetry and topology into dynamically controllable degrees of freedom. Graphene provides a paradigmatic platform for realizing this concept, where circularly polarized light has long been predicted to dynamically break time-reversal symmetry (TRS) and open a topologically nontrivial gap at the Dirac point. Despite extensive experimental efforts, direct observation of this Dirac gap-the defining spectroscopic signature of the dynamical TRS-breaking induced topological phase-has remained missing. Here we directly observe this light-induced Dirac gap in monolayer graphene. Time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy reveals that the gap emerges simultaneously with the optical field and exclusively under circularly polarized driving, directly linking its opening to dynamical TRS breaking. Together with Floquet theory, we identify the gap with a light-induced Haldane mass and reveal the associated nontrivial Floquet Berry curvature and Chern topology. By demonstrating dynamical TRS breaking in a prototypical non-magnetic material, our results establish optical driving as a route to ultrafast engineering of symmetry and topology, opening opportunities for dynamically tunable quantum matter beyond equilibrium.
item.dc:creator: Fei Wang, Xuanxi Cai, Wanying Chen, Xiao Tang, Jinze Li, Benshu Fan, Tianshuang Sheng, Jinxi Lu, Jiansong Li, Hongyun Zhang, Pu Yu, Peizhe Tang, Wenhui Duan, Angel Rubio, Zhiyuan Sun, Shuyun Zhou

item.title: Large deviations, gradient flows and fluctuating hydrodynamics for fractional diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2610.18182v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This work is a step towards a general understanding of fluctuations for systems of particles described at large scale by fractional diffusion. First, we derive formally a Large Deviation Principle for the empirical measure of mean-field interacting particles with a L{\'e}vy-type noise. In the case of independent particles, this unveils a generalized gradient flow structure at large scales. Second, we derive and solve numerically a stochastic Partial Differential Equation describing the fluctuating hydrodynamics of this system. The results compare well with direct numerical integration of the particles' dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Julien Barre (IDP), Hiroshi Horii

item.title: Moir\'e metals and continuum models beyond a single valley
item.description: arXiv:2610.40761v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive continuum models of moir\'e materials valid over the full monolayer Brillouin zone, as required for metals whose large Fermi surfaces are not confined to a single valley. To this end, we introduce an environment-resolved two-center approximation, in which each hopping amplitude depends not only on the distance between the orbitals it connects but also on its position within the moir\'e cell. Taking the local environment to be set by the disregistry of the two layers alone, these moir\'e couplings and their full set of harmonics can be learnt from commensurate bilayers at uniform stackings, without fitting. The method shows excellent agreement with ab initio band structures on moir\'e cells containing a few hundred atoms. Applied to twisted NbSe$_2$, it yields a continuum model in which moir\'e effects concentrate at the van Hove singularities, a single-particle starting point for studying moir\'e-tuned superconducting, charge-density-wave instabilities and their competition.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Albert, Andrew Klekovkin-Hardy, Valentin Cr\'epel

item.title: Preparation of a Laughlin-like fractional Chern insulator on a superconducting quantum processor
item.description: arXiv:2610.41017v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fractional Chern insulators (FCIs) are lattice analogues of fractional quantum Hall states, hosting topological order and fractionalized anyonic excitations. Their realization poses a demanding target for quantum simulation. Here, we realize a bosonic FCI on an IBM Nighthawk superconducting quantum processor using classically optimized variational circuits. We target a Laughlin-like state that is an exact zero-energy ground state of a long-range parent Hamiltonian on a torus, eliminating physical edges and providing a favorable geometry for accessing fractional quantum Hall physics in a small system. On a $4\times4$ qubit lattice, we prepare both the four-boson FCI ground state and a three-boson state hosting two quasiholes. Measurements of particle densities and correlations reproduce the characteristic structure of the target states, while reconstructed chiral magnetization currents resolve the circulating current pattern associated with the quasiholes. The preparation of these strongly correlated topological states with shallow circuits establishes a route toward the digital simulation and manipulation of fractionalized excitations, including measurements of topological invariants and anyonic braiding.
item.dc:creator: Kamil Dutkiewicz, B\'arbara Andrade, Geza Giedke, Tobias Grass

item.title: Induced Lorentzian geometry from the fermionic quantum metric
item.description: arXiv:2610.41138v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum geometry is conventionally understood in parameter or momentum space and need not be related to a geometry in configuration space. Here we show for Dirac fermions in a background electromagnetic field that an induced Lorentzian geometry is generated from the fermionic quantum metric. We study a Lorentz covariant phase space worldline path integral construction, whose application of the adiabatic theorem onto spin degrees of freedom leads to the appearance of the Berry phase at $O(\hbar)$, and the quantum metric at $O(\hbar^2)$ in the worldline action. Both the Feynman and retarded/advanced propagators are examined in 3+1 and 2+1 dimensions, whose different on-shell implementations lead to related quantum metrics; QED/QED${}_3$ and condensed matter Dirac theory are considered. An effective theory is found by integrating out the momenta degrees of freedom, which gives rise to an emergent Lorentzian metric in configuration space, whose perturbation to the flat metric is dependent on the quantum metric and the background field strength. Apart from the spin degrees of freedom encoded into the Berry phase, the effective theory describes a scalar particle moving in the induced quantum geometry. Phenomenological applications to the covariant geometry are further studied using spectral holonomy in a gapped 3-dimensional Dirac material.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Copinger, Pablo Morales

item.title: Quantifying Blinking Suppression and Probing Its Mechanism in PPD-Treated Single Quantum Dots
item.description: arXiv:2610.41285v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Colloidal semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) are highly promising materials for various applications, yet photoluminescence intermittency (blinking) remains a key obstacle to their practical use. While recent advances have enabled partial or complete suppression of this effect, both the degree of suppression and the mechanism by which it occurs are often difficult to establish. In the present work we analyse the blinking suppression of single CdSe/ZnS QDs after treatment with p-phenylenediamine (PPD), recently discovered by Yang et al. We revisit the blinking mechanism in this system and show that it is governed predominantly by the trapping mechanism, rather than by Auger ionization as previously proposed. For data analysis we apply a threshold-free two-dimensional criterion recently proposed by Podshivaylov and Frantsuzov. The criterion is based on the relative quantum yield estimator $\langle \hat{Q} \rangle^{(s)}$ and the decay-rate fluctuation parameter $\hat{\xi}$. We found that PPD treatment significantly increases the relative quantum yield and leads to only a modest increase in $\hat{\xi}$, indicating that the dominant effect of PPD is to shift the distribution of the non-radiative recombination rate toward lower values, rather than to eliminate its fluctuations. We further suggest a number of possible mechanisms of PPD-induced suppression and propose critical experiments for their verification.
item.dc:creator: Eduard A. Podshivaylov, Egor B. Kurgin, Changgang Yang, Guofeng Zhang, Pavel A. Frantsuzov

item.title: Helper-assisted quantum sensing with low dressed-state leakage
item.description: arXiv:2610.41404v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a two-qubit sensing protocol in which only a helper qubit is read out. Calibrated loading and unloading encode a transverse signal in the helper's phase, keep leakage out of a selected dressed-state band small, and return the sensor close to its idle ground state. We derive an information bound for a single sensor whose excitation stays below a prescribed budget, and simulate repeated operation with an uncertain coupling and finite-duration resets in a driven open-system model. At the tested settings, finite measurement records support estimation with infrequent resets. A helper flip at zero coupling, combined with a reversal of the coupling sign, suppresses a static helper offset shared across a record while retaining the signal, at a cost of about 27% of the no-offset information of a plain sequence of equal duration. Under slowly varying noise, averaging each cycle's likelihood over the correct noise law removes most of the added bias, and a wrong noise law can worsen the estimate. A selected directly read sensor with ideal controls and repeated nondemolition verification has the higher information rate. Any practical benefit of avoiding direct readout therefore requires a device-specific disturbance model.
item.dc:creator: Shirwan Abdullah

item.title: Pair density waves via interband pairing --- a perspective from superfluid weight
item.description: arXiv:2610.41687v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pair density waves (PDW) are superconducting states that exhibit a spatially modulated pairing order parameter, corresponding to Cooper pairs carrying finite center-of-mass momentum. While some recent studies have emphasized the role of quantum geometry in stabilizing PDW order in certain multiband systems, we here present a systematic investigation of an alternative, geometry-independent mechanism: PDW order driven purely by interband Cooper pairing. Using the superfluid weight (SW) as a diagnostic, we study two canonical models. The first is the classic Fulde-Ferrell model of an $s$-wave superconductor subject to a Zeeman splitting field, which realizes pure interband pairing between two rigidly shifted bands; the second is a spinless honeycomb-lattice model with nearest-neighbor $f$-wave pairing, a modified version of which was recently found to exhibit PDW instability in density-matrix renormalization-group simulations. In both models the SW receives no quantum geometric contribution at the mean-field level, yet it can be greatly suppressed or even turn negative, signaling a tendency toward pairing with spatial phase modulations. For the first model, we establish that the SW is increasingly suppressed as the Zeeman field grows, drastically turning negative upon the emergence of extensive gapless excitations, i.e., the Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces. For the honeycomb $f$-wave model, we demonstrate, both analytically and numerically, vanishing quantum-geometric SW and an invariably negative total SW. Our results thus establish the SW as a qualitative indicator of the tendency toward PDW order, and provide a microscopic rationale for the interband-pairing-driven PDW instability.
item.dc:creator: Yi-Jian Hu, Yi-Fan Jiang, Wen Huang

item.title: Creating functional nanostructures for vortex manipulation in superconducting Bi$_\text{2}$Sr$_\text{2}$CaCu$_\text{2}$O$_\text{8+x}$ thin films via focused He ion beam irradiation
item.description: arXiv:2610.41827v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+x}$ (Bi-2212) is a highly anisotropic high-temperature superconductor exhibiting unique vortex dynamics due to its layered structure. Precise nanoscale patterning of ultrathin Bi-2212 films remains challenging, limiting controlled studies of vortex pinning. Here, we employ 30 keV focused helium ion beam (He-FIB) irradiation to fabricate periodic arrays of columnar defects with 100 nm spacings in optimally-doped Bi-2212 thin films, thereby creating artificial vortex pinning centers. Magnetotransport measurements reveal pronounced vortex matching effects, evidenced by minima in magnetoresistance and peaks in critical current at commensurate magnetic fields. The angular dependence of magnetoresistance and critical current scale with an effective magnetic field, indicating strong confinement of pancake vortices along irradiation-induced tracks. These findings demonstrate the efficacy of He-FIB nanopatterning in modulating the superconducting properties in Bi-2212 thin films, providing a platform for fundamental studies of vortex matter and advancing prospects for device applications based on this highly anisotropic superconductor.
item.dc:creator: Bernd Aichner, Christoph Schmid, Sandra Keppert, Reinhold Kleiner, Edward Goldobin, Johannes D. Pedarnig, Dieter Koelle, Wolfgang Lang

item.title: Control-Noise Trade-offs in Industrially Integrated ${}^{28}\mathrm{Si}/\mathrm{SiGe}$ Spin-1/2 Qubits
item.description: arXiv:2610.41890v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scaling silicon spin qubits to fault-tolerant processors requires semiconductor foundry integration, yet it remains unclear how industrial fabrication and dense device integration affect qubit control and noise. Here we study ${}^{28}\mathrm{Si}/\mathrm{SiGe}$ electron spin-1/2 qubits fabricated using Intel's industry-compatible 300 mm process and incorporating micromagnets for electrically driven spin resonance, using a high-performance device fabricated in the RIKEN research cleanroom as a reference. Primitive $\pi/2$-gate fidelities reach the 99.99% level in the Intel devices, which also exhibit longer idle coherence, weaker low-frequency correlations and reduced qubit-to-qubit variability across several measured characteristics. In the present Intel devices, the micromagnets are integrated inline with the back-end-of-line (BEOL) contact routing, with their separation from the quantum well set through the vertical stack design. Relative to the reference, their larger separation contributes to weaker longitudinal and transverse magnetic-field gradients. The weaker longitudinal gradient suppresses the conversion of charge noise into qubit-frequency fluctuations, whereas the weaker transverse gradient reduces electrically driven spin-resonance efficiency and makes drive-dependent errors relevant at lower Rabi frequencies. Additional BEOL routing and metal levels required for two-dimensional arrays make such placement decisions increasingly consequential when scaling. These results establish an integration-level control-noise trade-off linking micromagnet placement within densely routed layouts to achievable gate performance, while very high-fidelity operation remains possible in industrially fabricated devices.
item.dc:creator: Leon C. Camenzind, Ik Kyeong Jin, Yi-Hsien Wu, Akito Noiri, Kenta Takeda, Takashi Nakajima, Takashi Kobayashi, Giordano Scappucci, Seigo Tarucha

item.title: Current-driven transient dynamics of magnetic-octupole domain walls in noncollinear antiferromagnets
item.description: arXiv:2610.42065v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Current-driven magnetic-octupole domain walls in noncollinear antiferromagnets are promising for fast spintronic devices, yet their transient dynamics are not yet fully understood. Here, we investigate spin-orbit-torque-driven domain-wall motion in Mn$_\text{3}$Sn using a multipole micromagnetic framework. The three symmetry-related 60{\deg} walls exhibit equivalent current-driven dynamics, unlike their field-driven motion. For a representative 60{\deg} wall, the post-pulse motion is governed by relaxation of the current-induced rotation of the surrounding octupole domains, with a characteristic time of approximately 33 ps quantitatively captured by a uniform-domain analytic model. By resolving spatially nonuniform texture dynamics beyond this analytic description, the simulations further reveal an additional slow relaxation in a composite 180{\deg} wall associated with the relative motion of its constituent walls. The post-pulse response also varies systematically with the exchange stiffness and magnetic anisotropies. These results identify distinct domain and internal-coordinate relaxation channels and establish the intrinsic time scales governing pulse-controlled positioning of magnetic-octupole domain walls in antiferromagnetic spintronic devices.
item.dc:creator: Myoung-Woo Yoo, Axel Hoffmann

item.title: Topologically Protected Edge States in a Single Flux Qubit
item.description: arXiv:2610.42114v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that topological edge states can be realized in a simple superconducting circuit composed of an inductively shunted flux qubit. The Josephson potential of that qubit forms a honeycomb lattice similar to the case of graphene. The additional shunting element produces a quartic potential along one flux direction, which effectively creates a boundary in flux space. We map analytically the low-energy dynamics of the circuit to an extended Su--Schrieffer--Heeger (SSH) chain, in which a quartic potential is added to the usual SSH Hamiltonian. This mapping is confirmed by numerical simulations of the full superconducting circuit. We argue that chiral symmetry still holds for the edge states of the extended model around a chiral point in parameter space. Close to this point, we numerically find that edge states in our superconducting circuit are topologically protected against perturbations that obey chiral symmetry, as is the case for charge noise. Our results show that topological effects previously thought to occur in multi-qubit systems, such as protection against decoherence, can also be found in much simpler single superconducting qubits.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Perez-Fernandez, Manuel Pino

item.title: Persistence of Unitary Almost Mathieu Operator Gaps Ten Dry Martinis, Five on the Rim
item.description: arXiv:2610.42120v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine exactly which gap labels are realized by open spectral gaps for the unitary almost Mathieu operator at every irrational frequency and all coupling constants ($0<\lambda_1,\lambda_2\leq1$). When both couplings are strictly less than one, every permitted gap label is realized by an open gap, including in the critical case ($\lambda_1=\lambda_2$). When at least one coupling equals one, both lifts of every odd winding label are realized by open gaps, whereas all even winding labels are collapsed. The proof combines quantitative almost reducibility and Aubry duality with a monotonicity principle for gap heights.
item.dc:creator: Dan S. Borgnia, Matthew Faust, Long Li

item.title: Baker--Akhiezer sections from Higgs bundles and Landau levels in hyperbolic band theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.42134v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As observed by Kienzle and the second author, rank-two $\mathcal{O}(3)$-twisted Higgs bundles on the projective line encode all hyperbolic crystals of genus two: the spectral curves are the unit cells, and the Hitchin fibers are the abelian Brillouin zones. In a uniform magnetic field of two flux quanta, the lowest Landau level is one-dimensional at every nonzero momentum, and, as found by Iengo and Li, its dimension jumps to two at the zero momentum. We identify the states of the lowest Landau level with the Baker--Akhiezer sections of the Higgs bundles, and their zeros, the vortices, with the Baker--Akhiezer divisors. A family of nonzero momenta limits to the zero momentum exactly when each of the two vortices approaches the image of the other under the spatial inversion, and the states of the jumped level are labeled by the directions of limiting. On the Higgs bundle side, the zero momentum is the point where the Hitchin fiber intersects the Hitchin section. Such a family of Higgs bundles limits to the Hitchin section, thereby crossing to a lower stratum of the \BB stratification, an example of the phenomenon investigated in terms of Baker--Akhiezer divisors by the first author with Figiel and Teschner.
item.dc:creator: Duong Dinh, Steven Rayan

item.title: Chiral Majorana hinge modes on a curved surface with magnetic impurities
item.description: arXiv:2310.09258v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Chiral Majorana modes, a key ingredient for topological quantum computation, arise on the surface of a three-dimensional time-reversal-invariant topological superconductor when a magnetic field induces a sign-changing surface mass. In practice, the orbital response of the superconductor tilts the surface spectrum and overwhelms the Zeeman term as the field grows. Here we show that magnetic impurities on a spherical surface can instead generate this mass term through their exchange coupling, so that only a weak field is required. The Ising surface Majorana modes mediate a ferromagnetic Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction, derived here on the curved surface, that orders the radial impurity moments into an inversion-breaking hedgehog at zero field. An axial field instead stabilizes a domain wall across which the radial magnetization reverses sign, leaving a single chiral Majorana mode along the equator and realizing an inversion-protected second-order topological superconductor.
item.dc:creator: Ilyoun Na, James G. McHugh, Sin\'ead M. Griffin, Luca Chirolli

item.title: Learning Hamiltonians for solid-state quantum simulators
item.description: arXiv:2603.02889v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a generalizable framework for identifying effective Hamiltonians directly from experimental data in solid-state quantum systems. Our unsupervised autoencoder-based approach incorporates the governing physics (here, the S-matrix formalism) directly into the decoder, enabling physically meaningful Hamiltonian inference without labeled Hamiltonian parameters. Through numerical experiments on a triple quantum dot chain, we demonstrate automated characterization of programmable solid-state simulators from transport measurements. The model accurately infers Hamiltonian parameters and generalizes beyond the training domain, while exhibiting finite capacity as the parameter space becomes increasingly broad or diverse. We further demonstrate robustness to noisy measurements and show that the model can be trained on transport data generated outside the Hamiltonian family assumed by the physics decoder, while still identifying meaningful effective parameters.
item.dc:creator: Jaros{\l}aw Paw{\l}owski, Mateusz Krawczyk

item.title: Quantum Batteries in two-dimensional material-based Josephson Junctions
item.description: arXiv:2605.22582v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the solid-state implementation of a Dicke-like quantum battery consisting of a two-dimensional material-based Josephson junction inductively coupled to a resonator, using graphene as a representative example. In this configuration, Andreev bound states naturally act as non-interacting, energetically non-degenerate two-level systems, and the setup allows for both single-photon and two-photon resonant processes. The coupling between the LC-circuit flux and the supercurrent through the junction gives rise to peculiar longitudinal interaction terms that have no counterpart in the conventional Dicke model. We demonstrate that these additional couplings can enhance energy storage for a proper range of parameters. The proposed architecture also enables an alternative, but comparable, charging protocol that relies on tuning the superconducting phase difference across the junction.
item.dc:creator: V. Varrica, G. Gemme, F. M. D. Pellegrino, E. Paladino, M. Sassetti, D. Ferraro

item.title: Scalar Spin Chirality from Dissipative Pumping and Lamb-Shift Precession
item.description: arXiv:2608.30324v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: How electrical driving generates and reverses scalar spin chirality in an interacting system with a real Hamiltonian and no magnetic flux remains a fundamental open question. We show that dissipative tunneling prepares an orbital pseudospin, while virtual charge fluctuations generate a noncollinear Lamb field that rotates it toward the chiral direction. Bias changes their relative orientation and thereby reverses the current. This reservoir-induced orbital Hanle effect converts a nonchiral orbital polarization into scalar spin chirality. Within the ground-state space, the circulating current is determined by the scalar spin chirality. Hierarchical-equations-of-motion calculations show that the low-bias reversal survives beyond the second-order weak-coupling description, while the quadratic growth of chirality after a sudden voltage switch identifies precession. More broadly, time-reversal-odd responses can emerge in open quantum systems from the interplay between dissipative state preparation and coherent precession.
item.dc:creator: YuanDong Wang, JianHua Wei

item.title: Making Weak Interlayer Excitons Absorb: Manipulating the Effective Oscillator Strength via Purcell Engineering of Critical Coupling
item.description: arXiv:2610.20307v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Interlayer excitons (IXs) in transition metal dichalcogenide bilayers possess unique dipolar properties, providing a path for exploring correlated many-body phases, electrically tunable dipole-dipole interactions, and long-range exciton transport. However, the large electron-hole separation underlying their dipolar character also results in a significantly reduced oscillator strength, limiting their direct optical interaction with light, and thus the direct probing of their dynamics and many-body interactions. Here, we show that by using Purcell engineering of critical coupling, a weak interlayer transition can absorb as strongly as the dominant intralayer transition, despite its much smaller intrinsic oscillator strength. Using this approach, in an open cavity architecture we demonstrate an order of magnitude IX absorption modulation in bilayer and trilayer MoS2, with doubling of the IX to A-exciton interaction strength weight from ~23% to ~53%. Furthermore, we demonstrate that in a tailored closed cavity architecture, the IX enhancement can reach beyond an order of magnitude, from ~5% to ~83% excitonic absorption, enabling IX absorption similar to intralayer excitons. An analytical description of the interaction is obtained via a closed-form transmission-line model which separates the excitonic and photonic contributions to the optical response, revealing how cavity architecture can be designed towards critical coupling. Our findings establish Purcell engineering of critical coupling as a general route to controlling and enhancing weak excitonic transitions.
item.dc:creator: Saroj Poudyal, Anabel Atash Kahlon, Michael Klein, Matan Meshulam, Yonatan Gershuni, Thomas Poirier, James H. Edgar, Mukesh Kumar, Seth Ariel Tongay, Itai Epstein

item.title: Nonlinear Dynamics of Rapidly Driven Systems
item.description: arXiv:2605.28996v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider systems characterized by the presence of a rapidly oscillating force. A general method is presented for the construction of the effective action governing the large-scale nonlinear dynamics of such systems order by order in inverse powers of the oscillation frequency $\omega$. The explicit expression for the effective Lagrangian is derived up to ${\cal O}(1/\omega^6)$ next-to-next-to-leading approximation in the strong-drive regime. The general structure of the high-frequency expansion reveals a broad class of nonlinear systems whose transition curves are identical to those of the linear Mathieu equation, which enables a fully nonperturbative stability analysis in the case of strong driving and nonlinearity. The method is generalized to velocity-dependent forces and configuration space with curvature, characteristic to systems with constraints. Several applications are discussed in detail, including the dynamical magnetic trapping of electric charges.
item.dc:creator: Afshin Besharat, Alexander A. Penin

item.title: Fluctuation-dissipation structure of quantum geometry
item.description: arXiv:2608.25006v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Geometry of quantum states is a fundamental research area with applications ranging from topological materials in condensed matter to variational algorithms in quantum information. Due to their relative simplicity, pure states are often studied, while mixed states are generally needed, e.g., to have nonzero temperature. Mixed-state geometry, however, is much more challenging and has so far lacked any structure relating distance and curvature, like the K\"ahler structure does for pure states. This work introduces that structure. We show that it has the physical meaning of fluctuation-dissipation---by identifying distance with fluctuations and curvature with linear response---and that it becomes the known structure for pure states, but is non-K\"ahler otherwise. This paints a simple picture that unifies fluctuation-dissipation and geometry of quantum states. It also applies on parameter spaces, as encountered in condensed matter or estimation theory. Our picture implies that the geometry contains all linear responses and fluctuations, proves the fluctuation-dissipation relation, explains that quantum geometry appears in any sum rule, and allows one to geometrically characterize generic transport behaviors. Closed and open systems are treated with equal ease.
item.dc:creator: Per Moosavi

item.title: Evidence for a charged vortex lattice in an exciton superfluid
item.description: arXiv:2610.37781v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Lattices of quantized vortices are a defining property of rotating superfluids and of type-II superconductors in magnetic fields. Realizing an analogous vortex lattice in an exciton superfluid-formed from bound electron-hole pairs-has remained challenging because excitons are electrically neutral. Building on previous theoretical studies of the low-energy excitations in an exciton superfluid, recent theory has predicted that in a strong magnetic field, a weakly charged exciton superfluid can stabilize a vortex-antivortex lattice arising from the mutual repulsion of fractionally charged vortex cores. Here we report evidence for this predicted vortex lattice in a bilayer exciton condensate by imaging its charged vortices with the scanning tunnelling microscope. The condensate forms between Landau levels of two graphene layers separated by a thin hexagonal boron nitride barrier in a perpendicular magnetic field. We find that the vortex lattice periodicity scales with the total excess charge and is insensitive to its distribution between the two layers, in quantitative agreement with theoretical predictions. Our observations provide evidence for phase coherence in an exciton superfluid system.
item.dc:creator: Ryan L. Lee, Jungwoo Lee, Viliam Va\v{n}o, Bo Zou, Cheng-Li Chiu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Allan MacDonald, Ali Yazdani
